usageNotes: Use this to create a named notification matcher that filters which events reach which notification targets (e.g. email, Gotify). The `name` field must follow the `pve-configid` format (alphanumeric plus hyphens, no spaces). Matchers are purely additive — no target receives notifications until a matcher explicitly references it via the `target` array.

examples.summary: Create a matcher that routes critical-severity backup-job failures to an email target, active only on business-hours calendar

params.name: backup-critical-alerts
params.comment: Route critical backup failures to on-call email during business hours

tips: The `match-field` values must be prefixed with `exact:` or `regex:` followed by `<field>=<value>` — omitting the prefix causes a validation error.
Setting `mode` to `any` means the matcher fires if ANY condition matches; the default `all` requires every condition to match simultaneously.
Use `invert-match: true` to build exclusion rules (e.g., suppress low-severity noise during maintenance windows).
Matchers are evaluated cluster-wide; changes take effect immediately without a service restart.
After creation, retrieve the matcher with GET /cluster/notifications/matchers/{name} to confirm the stored configuration.
